report:
Contrary to your initial assumption, medical evidence indicates that **yes, honey does help relieve acute cough in children aged 1 year and older**.

### Evidence Supporting Honey
* **Clinical Effectiveness:** Systematic reviews, including Cochrane reviews, demonstrate that honey reduces cough frequency and severity while improving sleep quality for both children and parents better than placebo, no treatment, or over-the-counter (OTC) cough medications like diphenhydramine (https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD007094.pub5/full, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37355498/).
* **Medical Guidelines:** The World Health Organization (WHO) and the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommend honey (typically 2.5–5 mL) as a safe remedy for coughs in children over age one, especially since OTC cough medicines show limited efficacy and carry risks for young children (https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/chest-lungs/Pages/Coughs-and-Colds-Medicines-or-Home-Remedies.aspx, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10570220/).

### Critical Safety Warning
Honey must **never** be given to infants under 12 months of age. Infants lack the mature gut flora needed to prevent *Clostridium botulinum* spores from growing, posing a risk of infant botulism, a serious paralysis-inducing illness (https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/chest-lungs/Pages/Coughs-and-Colds-Medicines-or-Home-Remedies.aspx).

### Conclusion
Evidence shows honey is an effective treatment for acute cough in children over 1 year of age, but it must strictly be avoided in infants under 12 months.
